html:
The Chichas were a people of the high valleys of southern Bolivia, around today's Tupiza and the Chichas province of Potosí, near the border with Argentina. In late pre-Hispanic times they formed a lordship within the Charcas world of the southern Andes, with the Qhara Qhara and Charka to the north.

Under the Inca they served as soldiers and guarded the empire's southern frontier against lowland peoples. After the Spanish conquest their land lay on the road from Potosí to the south, and it later became a rich silver and tin mining district. Their neighbours included the Omaguaca and the Atacameño.
